newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-FORMER PITCHING ACE MCLAIN CONVICTED IN THEFT.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-FORMER PITCHING ACE MCLAIN CONVICTED IN THEFT.

text.p: Former Detroit Tiger pitching star Denny McLain and a business associate were convicted Friday of stealing $3 million from the pension fund of a now defunct meat-packing company.
It took a federal jury less than three hours to find McLain and his partner, Roger Smigiel, guilty of theft, conspiracy, money-laundering and mail-fraud.

McLain was the last 30-game winner in the major leagues, winning 31 games in 1968 as he led the Tigers to a World Series championship and was given the Cy Young award as the best pitcher of the season.

After retiring from baseball, McLain was convicted of racketeering, extortion and cocaine possession in 1985. He served only two years of his 23-year sentence after an appeals court ruled he had not received a fair trial.

In the current case, prosecutors said McLain, 52, Smigiel, 45, and Jeffrey Egan, 36, raided the $12.5 million pension fund of Peet Packing Co, located in the central Michigan town of Chesaning, after buying the company in 1994. The company closed in June 1995, putting about 200 people out of work.

Prosecutors said McLain and Smigiel used the money stolen from the fund to pay off loans used to buy the packing company as well as to purchase a condominium in Puerto Rico, a Harley-Davidson classic motorcycle and a membership in the Great Lakes Country Club.

Egan, of the Detroit suburb of Bloomfield Hills, was the government's key witness in the case. As the trio's financial adviser, he said he devised the scheme to transfer money out of the fund using two shell companies.

Egan, who earlier pleaded guilty to a single count of pension fund theft, said he carried out the plan with the full knowledge of McLain and Smigiel. Defence attorneys argued that McLain and Smigiel were duped by Egan.
McLain and Smigiel could be sentenced to prisons terms of five to 20 years.
